title: 221. two psych majors tell ALL: GPAs, grad school, & so much more!
description_html: In this week’s episode, we are sharing part 2 of our tips for being a psychology major! I am once again joined by my friend (and fellow psych major at UPenn!) to discuss even more things you absolutely need to know about majoring in psychology in college.
talk_about: how important your grades really are
getting funding & grants for psych research
having your research published as an undergrad
why you should attend psych conferences
how to make your CV stand out
applying for graduate schools for psych
what we were glad we did as psych majors…
…& what we wish we did differently
mentioned_html:
• ⁠Psychology major advice pt. 1⁠

  • ⁠Penn Psychology⁠

  • ⁠ADAA Conference⁠

  • ⁠ABCT Conference⁠

  • ⁠Olivia’s email⁠
guests: olivia, upenn psychology major and president of penn undergraduate psychology society
summary: sadie and her friend olivia, both graduating psychology majors at upenn, share part two of their advice for psych students. they discuss how much grades really matter (especially in-major gpa), choosing meaningful extracurriculars over fomo, getting involved in research early, and applying for small grants even as undergrads. they cover practical steps like building a cv from day one, writing a thesis, presenting posters at conferences, and networking by providing value first. both applied to grad school senior year (unusual but worth it for the experience) and emphasize that success in psychology comes more from what you do outside the classroom—research, volunteering, mentorship—than from coursework alone.
quote: no one knows your application like you do.
quote_display: NO ONE knows your application like YOU do.
